clue.text: Father returns quietly to fish and gets shot, of course

indicators.note: returns says the word for father comes back the other way round

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A dad comes home quietly from fishing and then goes off shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns PA into AP. 'of course' points to a golf course: this is the shot played on to the green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the stroke that sends the ball onto the green is called by this name.

clue.text: Notice a new sport requires circuit accessories

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: new says the letters of sport come in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An advertisement says a new sport needs equipment for a track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SPORT into PTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plug converters fitted to electrical circuits are small accessories.

clue.text: Moriarty for chairman ?

definitions.meaning: the arch-villain of the Sherlock Holmes stories, an academic by title
one who holds a university chair

explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's enemy Moriarty is styled an academic title, and a university chair is held by such an academic.

clue.text: Admitted to having had property

explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, and to own is to possess.

clue.text: Bore made a call about rising artist

explanation.surface: A dull person cried out about an artist who was getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RA into AR, and 'about' puts it inside CRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, to transport, a synonym.

clue.text: Rising from a trail

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: Something gets up off a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising, as a noun, is a climb upward, the same as this word.

clue.text: A little drink doesn't matter much

definitions.meaning: weak beer, literally a minor drink

explanation.definitionFit: Weak beer is the literal sense; figuratively the phrase means something trivial.

clue.text: Way to get in, if guard loses his head

parts.note: a sentry guards a post

explanation.surface: To get inside, a guard has to be decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' drops the S from SENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A door or gate, a means of access, is a synonym.

clue.text: For the Welsh line, change at Stroud

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of Stroud

explanation.surface: A rail passenger is told to change at Stroud for the Welsh line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges STROUD; 'line' is a royal dynasty, not a railway. Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty of Henry VII had Welsh origins, so it is the Welsh line of monarchs.

clue.text: This property may need a fence

definitions.text: This property may need a fence

parts.words: This property may need a fence
parts.note: fence is read as a receiver of ... goods rather than a garden barrier

explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a dealer in stolen goods.

clue.text: Part of mast? Take bill round to the Navy

parts.note: ac is short for account, a bill
a round shape like a ring gives the letter O
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
N is the abbreviation for Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to carry a bill around to the Navy, with a ship's mast in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast here is not a ship's spar but the fallen nuts of forest trees, eaten by pigs; the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the collective name for fallen beech and oak nuts, and the oak's nut is one of them.

clue.text: Withdrew transporter sent back by Edward

clue.text: Punishment rated improper by economist

explanation.walkthrough: 'improper' rearranges RATED to TREAD. Prisoners in Victorian gaols were made to walk a wheel as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The prison wheel walked by convicts was a recognised penal labour in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Better bird in production

definitions.meaning: one who lays a bet, a gambler

clue.text: Very nosy was this dramatist's hero

definitions.text: Very nosy was this dramatist's hero

clue.text: Points to North-what a match!

clue.text: Upset by data, I get confused

clue.text: Joint with food for dropout
